comment: Path globs to risk tier, read by np_risk_tiers.py and consumed by the spec-guard CI job (F7/#253). THIS TAXONOMY IS A SYNTHESIS, NOT A CITATION. No published standard enumerates high-risk code paths: CIS says 'extra sensitive code or configuration' without defining it, Google's Building Secure and Reliable Systems says 'safety implications', SLSA says 'security-relevant properties'. Every organization invents its own list, and this is ours. Do not cite it as though it came from a standard.
precedence: LAST MATCH WINS, mirroring CODEOWNERS. Position in the `rules` array is what decides, NOT specificity -- a broader glob placed lower overrides a narrower one above it. This is the opposite of most people's intuition. Practical consequence: standard-tier globs go FIRST and high-tier globs go LAST, and appending a broad standard glob at the bottom silently downgrades everything it matches. A test asserts that no standard rule appears after a high one.
matching: fnmatch, whose `*` is NOT path-aware -- it translates to regex `.*` and already crosses `/`. Any wildcard here reaches arbitrary depth, so `docs/**` and `docs/*` behave identically. Written with `**` for readability only.

content-overlay knowledge pages
skill reference depth, not the skill body
test-only changes; the suite is its own gate

CI config; also the only place repo secrets are in scope
the PII redaction path
the secret/PII publication gate
layer path resolution; a wrong root reads or writes the wrong repo
installers mutate the machine outside the repo
reads and stores credentials
